question:
A researcher is studying how electrical activity propagates across the heart. In order to do this, he decides to measure the rate at which an action potential moves within various groups of cardiac muscle tissue. In particular, he isolates fibers from areas of the heart with the following characteristics:

A) Dysfunction leads to fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
B) Dysfunction leads to increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
C) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex
D) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on electrocardiogram

Which of the following is the proper order of these tissues from fastest action potential propagation to slowest action potential propagation.?
analysis: To determine the order of action potential propagation speed in cardiac tissues, we need to understand the characteristics of each dysfunction: A) Fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat suggest an issue with the AV node, typically seen in Mobitz Type II AV block. B) Increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat are characteristic of Mobitz Type I (Wenckebach) AV block, also involving the AV node. C) Tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex indicates a ventricular origin, such as ventricular tachycardia, where conduction is slower. D) Tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on ECG is indicative of atrial flutter, involving rapid atrial activity. The order of conduction speed from fastest to slowest is: atrial tissue (D) > AV node (A and B) > ventricular tissue (C). Therefore, the correct order is D > C > A > B.
